contexts.text: The sense of the letter is a receptacle...
That the Divine good may have in (these appearances) a kind of receptacle.
Vessels = whatever serves as receptacles; as scientifics relatively to truths...
This receptacle is the memory.
This receptacle is the interior memory.
The Natural serves the Rational as a receptacle.
For ultimates are receptacles of their priors.
The Corporeal itself is nothing but a receptacle of sensations.
Wherever there is a receptacle in the Natural. Signified.
As a sack is a receptacle of corn, so is a scientific a receptacle of good. Explained.

Man's Natural is distinguished into receptacles. In each receptacle there is a certain General... Every such General, together with its particulars and singulars, has its own receptacle... With a regenerate man these receptacles are as many as are the general truths with him; and each receptacle corresponds to a certain Society in Heaven.
That the receptacles of good and truth are completely desolated. Signified, Explained.
For the body, or the whole man... is a receptacle of life from the Lord; thus a receptacle of good.
These receptacles (of good and truth) are said to die, when there is nothing of spiritual life within.
A total submission... of these receptacles. Signified. By the receptacles are meant the very forms of man...
For the External... is the receptacle into which the Internal inflows...
For the understanding is the receptacle of truth; and the will is the receptacle of good.
These (scientifics) are the receptacles of the influx of good and truth... and the Natural is the general receptacle.
For the external man is the receptacle of the truth and good from the internal. If the receptacle is not accommodated, it does not receive anything which inflows from within. AC 8452.
Heaven is nothing but a receptacle of truth Divine... AC 9415.
The table = the receptacle of celestial things... In the opposite, a receptacle of such things as are in Hell. Illustrated.
The conjunction of this receptacle with the good of love. Signified.
For a receptacle must be accommodated to the Things which are to be received.
The ultimate receptacle of the heavenly marriage. Signified.
For love is the receptacle of all things of Heaven...
An Angel is a receptacle, and thence is a Heaven in the least form.
For innocence is the receptacle of the truth of faith and the good of love.
That innocence is the receptacle of all things of Heaven...
The sole receptacle of good is truth.
Natural heat serves spiritual heat as a receptacle...
The spiritual atmospheres are receptacles of... love and wisdom... But the natural atmospheres... are receptacles of the fire and light of their sun. DLW 183.
The organic substances which are the receptacles... of the thoughts and affections in the brains.
For the atmospheres are the receptacles of heat and light; and heat and light are the receptacles of love and wisdom. DLW 223.
Nature which is dead; and yet is a receptacle of the Divine...
For the natural degree is the general receptacle of the light of (these degrees).
The seed which is from the father is the first receptacle of life; but such a receptacle as it was with the father...
That two receptacles and habitations of the Lord have been created with man, which are called the will and the understanding... DLW 395.
For man and Angel are... only a receptacle, in itself dead...

In every human embryo the Lord forms two receptacles... a receptacle of the Divine love for the future will of the man; and a receptacle of the Divine wisdom for his future understanding. DP 328:5. DP 328:6.
The image of God is the receptacle of God; (thus) it is the receptacle of the love and wisdom from God in him...
Man is a receptacle of God; and, as God is love itself and wisdom itself, man is a receptacle of these; and a receptacle becomes an image of God as he receives.
The soul is not life; but is the proximate receptacle of life from God.
(The intelligence of the husband is the receptacle of the wife's love...)
What is life but love and wisdom? and what is nature but their receptacle...

Hence there are in man two receptacles of life; one, which is the receptacle of good, is called the will; and the other, which is the receptacle of truth, is called the understanding; (therefore) the will is the receptacle of love; and the understanding is the receptacle of wisdom.
That the infinite is in finites as in receptacles. Explained.

It is through these degrees that all posteriors are receptacles of their priors; and these again of their priors; and thus, in order, are the receptacles of the primitives, of which the Sun consists; and thus that Unites are the receptacles of the infinite. Explained.
Man was created a receptacle of (the Divine love and the Divine wisdom); and therefore he was created into order.
The end of creation was... man, in whom God could dwell as in His receptacle.
(The salvation of man) cannot be effected unless he prepares himself to be a receptacle...
God could not redeem men unless... the Human formed itself into a receptacle...
In proportion as man (believes in God, and loves the neighbour) from natural power, in the same proportion he makes himself a receptacle of the Divine omnipotence.
These (laws of order) the Lord fulfilled, and thus made Himself a receptacle of the Divinity...
Still, man by (natural faith and charity) prepares himself to be a receptacle of the Lord...
(Natural) heat and light have nothing of life in them, but they serve (spiritual heat and light) as receptacles; as instrumental causes are wont to do their principal ones...
That man is not life; but is a receptacle of the life from God. General article.
Memory has been given to man in order to be a receptacle...
The receptacle of the good of love is the will; and the receptacle of the truth of faith is the understanding.

Hence there are two receptacles of life... called the understanding and the will; the understanding being the receptacle of the Divine truth, and the will the receptacle of the Divine good; or, what is the same, the understanding is the receptacle of wisdom from the Lord; and the will is the receptacle of love from Him. AE 790:12.
Man's thought is the receptacle of truth; and his will is the receptacle of good. AE 831:4. AE 837:4.
Every natural thing is a general receptacle of spiritual things...

The will is the receptacle of man's love; and the understanding is the receptacle of his wisdom; and that which is a receptacle of the love, is also a receptacle of all the affections... A receptacle of love is mentioned, because love is not possible with man except in a recipient form, which is substantial.
Regarded in itself, the will is not love, but is a receptacle of it; and such a receptacle as not only receives love, but also imbues its states, and puts on forms according to them...
That the Lord created, and afterwards forms with man, a receptacle of love, which is his will; and adjoins thereto a receptacle of wisdom, which is his understanding. Explained.
On the formation of man in the womb by influx into these two receptacles. Explained.
2. That He conjoins Himself in these two receptacles... Explained.
4. 3. Therefore the initiaments of the life of beasts are not receptacles of the Lord's love and wisdom; but are receptacles of natural affection and knowledge.
5. That one receptacle is for the will of the future man, and the other is for his understanding; and yet there is nothing whatever of will and understanding present at the formation. Explained.
5. That after birth the will becomes the receptacle of love, and the understanding the receptacle of wisdom. Explained.

2. The reason the will and understanding are called receptacles, is that the will is not an abstract spiritual something; but is a subject substantiated and formed for the reception of love from the Lord...
